# Copilot Instructions

## Product

This is the **Whitbread Premier Inn Front-End Applications** monorepo — the customer-facing web platform for Premier Inn, one of the UK's largest hotel chains.

Three applications live here:
- **Premier Inn** (`apps/next-apps/premier-inn`) — main hotel booking experience (search, rooms, guest details, payment, confirmation, amendments)
- **Business Booker** (`apps/next-apps/business-booker`) — corporate/business travel booking portal
- **CCUI** (`apps/next-apps/ccui`) — Customer Care UI for internal agents

Key domains: hotel search, booking checkout flow, amendments/cancellations, Auth0 authentication, account dashboard, Unleash feature flags, i18n via next-i18next.

---

## Tech Stack

- **Next.js** 14.x (Pages Router), **React** 18.x, **TypeScript** 5.x (strict mode)
- **GraphQL** + `graphql-request` — primary data fetching; **TanStack React Query** 5.x — server state
- **Chakra UI** 2.x wrapped by `@whitbread-eos/atoms`; **Emotion** for CSS-in-JS
- **React Hook Form** + Yup — forms; **Axios** — REST; **Firebase** 10.x — backend services
- **Auth0** (`@auth0/nextjs-auth0`), **Unleash** (`@unleash/nextjs`), **Framer Motion**
- **Lerna** 9.x + **Nx** — monorepo orchestration and task caching
- **Babel** — component library transpilation; **GraphQL Code Generator** — type generation
- **Jest** 29.x + **React Testing Library** — unit/integration; **Playwright** — e2e
- **ESLint** 8.x, **Prettier** 2.x, **Husky** + **Commitizen** (conventional commits)

---

## Project Structure

```
apps/next-apps/
  premier-inn/        # Main booking app
  business-booker/    # Corporate booking app
  ccui/               # Customer Care UI

pi-components-catalog/   # Shared @whitbread-eos/* packages (atomic design)
  atoms/              # @whitbread-eos/atoms — base UI (Chakra wrappers)
  molecules/          # @whitbread-eos/molecules
  organisms/          # @whitbread-eos/organisms
  utils/              # @whitbread-eos/utils
  api/                # @whitbread-eos/api
  layout/             # @whitbread-eos/layout
  config/             # @whitbread-eos/config
  pages/
    amend/            # @whitbread-eos/amend
    confirmation/     # @whitbread-eos/confirmation
    dashboard/        # @whitbread-eos/dashboard
    guest-details/    # @whitbread-eos/guest-details
    payment/          # @whitbread-eos/payment
```

Each app's `src/` follows this layout:
`components/`, `hooks/`, `pages/`, `page-helper/`, `services/`, `store/`, `queries/`, `types/`, `utils/`, `mocks/`, `styles/`, `theme/`, `firebase/`, `lib/`

---

## TypeScript Path Aliases

All apps use `baseUrl: ./src`. Always use these aliases — never deep relative paths:

| Alias | Maps to |
|---|---|
| `~components/*` | `src/components/*` |
| `~hooks/*` | `src/hooks/*` |
| `~services/*` | `src/services/*` |
| `~store/*` | `src/store/*` |
| `~queries/*` | `src/queries/*` |
| `~types/*` | `src/types/*` |
| `~utils/*` | `src/utils/*` |
| `~mocks/*` | `src/mocks/*` |
| `~styles/*` | `src/styles/*` |

---

## Code Conventions

- **Prettier**: single quotes, 2-space indent, 100-char line width, trailing commas (ES5), semicolons on
- **Imports**: `@whitbread-eos/*` and `~*` aliases first, then relative — enforced by ESLint import plugin
- **No `console.log`** in committed code (ESLint warns)
- **Commits**: use `yarn commit` for the Commitizen CLI wizard (conventional commits enforced via Husky)
- **Atomic design**: atoms → molecules → organisms → pages. Lower levels must not import from higher levels
- **SVG icons** in `atoms/src/assets/icons/` are auto-generated by `svgr` — do not edit manually
- After modifying component libraries, run `yarn build:atomic:components` before starting apps

---

## Common Commands

```bash
# Dev servers
yarn start:pi                    # Premier Inn
yarn start:ccui                  # CCUI
yarn start:bb                    # Business Booker

# Build
yarn build:atomic:components     # Build all shared libs first
yarn build:pi / build:ccui / build:bb

# Test
yarn test                        # All packages
yarn test:ci                     # CI mode (coverage + bail)

# Quality
yarn lint:fix                    # Auto-fix lint
yarn type-check                  # TypeScript across all packages
yarn type-generate               # Regenerate GraphQL types

# Per-app (run from app directory)
yarn check-integrity             # type-check + lint:fix + test + build
```

# JavaScript & TypeScript Copilot Instructions

## Copilot Code Review Behavior (High Priority)

These rules apply **only to GitHub Copilot code reviews** (PR review summaries, review comments).

### Jira Context Awareness
When reviewing a pull request:

- First look in the **PR description** for a block delimited by:
  <!-- jira-context:start -->
  ...
  <!-- jira-context:end -->

- If not present in the PR description, look for the same block in **PR comments**.

- Treat the content inside this block as the **authoritative Jira ticket context**.

- Use this context to:
  - Evaluate alignment between code changes and ticket intent
  - Identify scope mismatches
  - Flag unrelated or suspicious changes

- If the Jira context block is missing, **explicitly state this** and base the review only on code.

---

## AI Developer Profile

- Act as a senior full-stack developer with deep JavaScript and TypeScript knowledge.
- Prioritize simplicity, readability, maintainability, and performance.

---

## Technical Stack & Repository Awareness (No Hardcoding)

- Do not assume tool versions (Node, package manager, frameworks).
- Infer tooling and scripts from repository sources in this order:
  1) `README.md`
  2) `package.json` and workspace tooling files
  3) `.github/workflows/*`
- Prefer existing dependencies rather than introducing new ones.
- If build/test/lint scripts are unclear, state this explicitly and provide safe generic guidance.

---

## Language Guidelines

### General Coding Principles
- Less code is better; avoid unnecessary abstraction.
- Make minimal, focused changes.
- Keep logic readable and explicit.

### DRY & Functional Style
- Prefer functional, immutable patterns where practical.
- Keep side effects isolated and explicit.

### Early Returns & Conditionals
- Use early returns to reduce nesting.
- Prefer clarity over cleverness.
- Avoid overly complex ternaries.

### Naming & Constants
- Use descriptive names.
- Prefix event handlers with `handle` (e.g., `handleClick`).
- Prefer constants and clear type definitions.

### Documentation
- Use JSDoc in JavaScript when helpful.
- Do not use JSDoc in TypeScript unless required; rely on types.

---

## Copilot Code Review \u2013 House Style

### How to structure the Pull Request overview
When summarizing a pull request, format the **Pull request overview** using these sections and the guiding questions beneath each. Use clear bullets and short sentences.
Commit messages and PR descriptions may be of varying quality and accuracy. Where that is the case, give more weight to the actual changes and mention that fact in the PR overview.

#### 1. Maintainability
- Is this code maintainable?
- Is maintainability improving or deteriorating?
- Identify duplication and suggest refactoring.

#### 2. Complexity
- Is complexity increased?
- Suggest simpler alternatives.
- Note algorithmic complexity changes if relevant.

#### 3. Testability
- Are tests present or updated?
- List specific missing tests (edge cases, async/error paths).
- Recommend scaffolding if risk is high.

#### 4. Performance & Efficiency
- Highlight hot paths, bundle size impact, and regressions.
- Suggest measurable optimizations when justified.

#### 5. Consistency & Standards
- Check alignment with linting and project conventions.
- Flag deviations and propose precise fixes.

#### 6. Security
- Identify potential vulnerabilities (e.g., XSS, injection, CSRF).
- Ensure no secrets are introduced.
- Confirm sensitive data is handled appropriately.

### Review Tone & Format
- Be concise, actionable, and specific.
- Prefer bullet points over long paragraphs.
- Include code snippets only when necessary.
- If context is missing, explicitly state it.

### Out of Scope & Pitfalls
- Do not suggest large architectural rewrites unless clearly necessary.
- Avoid vague statements; provide one concrete suggestion per issue.

---

## Atoms Component Development Requirements

### Story Coverage Requirements

**Every component in `pi-components-catalog/atoms/src/components/` MUST have a corresponding `.stories.tsx` file.**

When reviewing PRs or creating new components:

1. **New components**: Require a co-located `.stories.tsx` file in the same component folder (e.g., `Button.component.tsx` + `Button.stories.tsx`)
2. **Modified components**: Update stories for prop changes, new variants, behavior changes, and defaults
3. **Deleted components**: Remove the matching `.stories.tsx` file
4. **Coverage mismatch**: Flag missing, stale, or misnamed stories as a PR blocker

### Story Coverage Review Checklist

- Verify each changed component in `atoms/src/components/` has a matching story file.
- Verify story args still match the current component props and defaults.
- Verify new visual states or variants introduced in code are represented in stories.
- Verify deleted or renamed components do not leave orphaned story files.

---

## Storybook CSF3 Story Authoring Guardrails (Atoms)

Apply these rules for all new stories and all CSF2 to CSF3 migrations in `pi-components-catalog/atoms`.

### Core Storybook Pattern

- Use CSF3 only.
- Use explicit meta typing:
  - `const meta: Meta<typeof Component> = { ... }`
  - `export default meta`
  - `type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>`
- Do not use `ComponentMeta` or `ComponentStory`.
- Do not import from `@storybook/addon-actions`.
- Do not use `action: 'eventName'` shorthand in `argTypes`.
- For callback props, set `control: false` and provide clear descriptions.

### ArgTypes Completeness

- Every prop from the component props interface must have an `argTypes` entry.
- Every `argTypes` entry must include:
  - `description`
  - an appropriate control strategy
- Control mapping rules:
  - string -> `text`
  - boolean -> `boolean`
  - enum or union -> `radio` (up to 5 options), otherwise `select`
  - number -> `number` (add min or max where applicable)
  - function callbacks -> `control: false`
  - object or complex -> `object`

### Story Structure and Naming

- Keep story sections in this order when applicable:
  - Basic Usage
  - Variants
  - Sizes
  - States
  - Configuration
  - Edge Cases
- Naming conventions:
  - `Default` first with minimal required args
  - `WithFeature` for additive features
  - `[Variant]Variant` for visual variants
  - `[Size]Size` for size presets
  - `[State]State` for interactive states
  - `With[EdgeCase]` for edge cases
- Prefer args-only stories.
- Use `render` only when wrappers, layout, or controlled state are required.

### Hooks and Render Safety

- Never use hooks directly inside anonymous story `render` functions.
- If state is needed, create a named wrapper component and render that wrapper from the story.

### Lint-Safe Helpers

- If a no-op callback is needed, define one reusable `noop` constant near the top of the story file and reuse it.
- Keep stories lint-clean and type-clean.

### Parameters and Docs Quality

- Preserve existing Figma design links.
- Include component docs description in `parameters.docs.description.component`.
- Do not remove useful existing `parameters` entries unless they are obsolete.

### Definition of Done

- No ESLint errors.
- No TypeScript errors.
- No forbidden Storybook imports or legacy CSF2 typings.
- Full prop to `argTypes` coverage.
- Story naming and section grouping follow this standard.

### Story Review Priorities

Use this section for **Storybook story migration/authoring reviews only**. Prioritize:

- missing `argTypes` coverage (all props represented, with descriptions and valid controls)
- hook misuse in `render` (hooks only in named wrapper components)
- forbidden Storybook patterns/imports (CSF2 typing, addon-actions import, `action:` shorthand)
- missing docs or design metadata (`parameters.docs.description.component`, Figma links)
- weak or unclear story naming (must follow naming and section conventions)

Request concrete fixes with file-level examples and expected end state; avoid generic comments.
